https://2gis.ae/dubai/interesting.visible_text: Where to go in UAE – A list of interesting places for tourists — A guide by 2GIS ............................................................................. ............................................................................. ............................................................................. ............................................................................. ............................................................................. ............................................................................. ............................................................................. ............................................................................. ............................................................................. ............................................................................. ............................................................................. ............................................................................. ............................................................................. Search Routes Friends Guide Interesting in UAE Find out where to go in UAE: interesting places, best attractions, places for recreation and entertainment. Ideas for walks and cultural activities. Top Attractions: the Tallest, the Largest, the Fastest Almost everything in the UAE is the largest, the coolest, or the most expensive in the world. Dubai is the city of the world’s tallest buildings, the tallest Ferris wheel, and the world's largest flower garden. If not, the winner is probably not far away. The neighbouring emirate and the capital Abu Dhabi is home to the world’s fastest roller coaster and the world’s largest carpet. Here is the list of record-breaking attractions in the UAE. Michelin-starred Restaurants in Dubai Dubai boasts a dazzling line-up of Michelin-starred restaurants — here’s the full list for 2025. Cover photo: Trèsind Studio. A Trip to Abu Dhabi: Ferrari, Louvre, the Largest Mosque It takes about 1–2 hours to get from Dubai to Abu Dhabi, the capital of the UAE. The reasons to go are numerous: the UAE's largest mosque, the Louvre Abu Dhabi, featuring art from Van Gogh to Ai Weiwei, the fastest roller coaster in the world and a cafe serving cappuccino topped with real gold. Great Photos from Dubai: Locations, Tips, Lifehacks Want to bring great photos from Dubai? @maximdenisenko , a photographer working in Dubai spends all his free time looking for photography locations. In this guide Maxim Denisenko shows the most picturesque beaches and secret spots with a great view and gives some tips for avoiding crowds and getting the best shots. Сlick on the photos to see the whole picture! Cheap and Yummy: Shawarma, Kebab, Falafel Dubai is not only a melting pot of cultures, but also a frying pan full of different foods from all over the world. Immigrants bring their culinary traditions to Dubai, creating a diverse, exotic, and very affordable food scene. Here are some of the best street food spots and eateries with an average bill of 15–60 AED. Fancy Enough: Mid-range Priced Restaurants and Cafés Here are some great restaurants and cafés that do not cost a fortune. From authentic Emirati cuisine in an old courtyard to fresh seafood at the beach. An average bill for this selection is 60–150 AED. A Special Dinner: the Best Views, the Finest Cuisine Many of the high-end Dubai restaurants offer not only world-class cuisine, but also a unique experience of being on top of the world or surrounded by the sea. An average bill for this selection is 200–500 AED. Neighbourhoods: Where to Stay and Where to Go Dubai is a diverse and spread-out city. To the South-West lies the modern Dubai: posh beaches of the Palm, glamorous villas of Jumeirah, futuristic skyscrapers of Dubai Marina, JLT, and the Dubai Downtown. To the North-East lies the old Dubai: Deira and Bur Dubai, separated by the Creek. Here is our guide to Dubai neighbourhoods. Adventure Time: Fly, Dive, and Discover Wonders If you think Dubai is only for shopping and lazing on the beach with a cocktail, you’ve probably never tried skydiving or flyboarding, never seen camel races, or a wrecked ship at the bottom of the sea. Here are some adventures available in Dubai: from safe and suitable for the whole family to risky and real. The Best Public Beaches: from Popular to Secret Check out 8 great public beaches in Dubai: from the most popular and vibrant to “secret” and solitary. Almost all public beaches in Dubai have no entrance fee (except Al Mamzar). The Best Private Beaches: Pools, Cocktails, DJs For more comfortable and glamorous beach time head for numerous private beaches. Private beaches in Dubai are typically attached to shoreline hotels and are free to use for hotel guests, but outsiders can get a day pass for a fee (100–500 AED). A sunbed is usually included as well as access to a pool. Cheaper on weekdays. Beaches are open from 8–10 AM till sunset. Some private beaches throw parties after dark. Many have a Ladies Day with discounts for ladies. Prices and conditions change often, so checking and booking in advance is strongly recommended. A Gastro Trip to Abu Dhabi: The Best Restaurants From authentic Emirati cuisine to the best steaks, from lunch at the fish market to dinner in one of the most romantic restaurants. The Best Bars: Drinks, Music, Views A fancy bar in Dubai must have a view — the poshest places sell not only cocktails, but also the feeling of having the city at your feet. This objective comes with a price tag to match. Most of the bars in Dubai have a happy hour (usually from 5pm to 8pm) and a ladies’ day on Tuesday. A ladies’ day does not mean that men are not allowed, it simply means that female guests get complimentary drinks. Cover photo: Galaxy. Souks: Gold, Spices, Rugs The souks (markets) in Bur Dubai (Textile, Gold and Spice Souk) date back to the early XXth century when Dubai was the trading centre of the whole Gulf Coast. Nowadays the souks in Dubai have become quite touristy — but it is still a chance to get a glimpse and some experience of traditional Dubai lifestyle. And also buy almost everything: from souvenirs to gold, from fresh fish to used cars. Dubai for Kids: Waterparks, Dolphins, Trampolines Dubai is a great place to take kids to. Here are some experiences your kid will always remember: from roller coasters to trampolines, from sunken chambers with sharks and treasures to meeting the real penguines, from an amusement park where everything is made of LEGO to a cafe where everything — including burgers — is made of cake. Oh and you do not have to be a kid literally and officially to enjoy most of the places from this collection. Tip: plan your time ahead and buy tickets online — usually it will be much cheaper. To avoid queues at popular family destinations keep in mind that Sunday is a working day in the UAE and Friday is a holiday. The History of Dubai: from Pearls to Oil How did Dubai become the city we know? Before the oil there were pearls, before the skyscrapers there were narrow lanes and wind towers. Here are some points of Dubai history — and some walls that can tell a story or be a vivid display. Fantastic Beasts: Horses, Camels, Flamingos Giant aquariums and wildlife sanctuaries, camel races and stable tours, sloths and bats living in a simulated rainforest and a garden of thousands of butterflies… Meet your favourite animals from all over the world. A Day in Downtown Dubai: Eat, Walk, Shop You come to a new city, check into a hotel, and immediately go to the centre to see the most famous attractions. In Dubai, that means going to Downtown Dubai featuring the Burj Khalifa, the Dubai Mall, the Dubai Fountain and the futuristic Dubai Opera, fancy boulevards and posh nightclubs. Here are some ideas for a day in Downtown Dubai: from breakfast and dinner with a view, to shopping, to sightseeing. 15 Most Instagrammable Cafes Presenting a selection of the most visually outstanding cafes in the city of awe-inspiring designs. Here are the dreamy pink dollhouses, real jungles, and light minimalistic interiors. And, of course, pretty desserts and coffees. Shopping Malls: indoor and outdoor There are dozens of shopping malls in Dubai, each accommodating hundreds of shops, not to mention restaurants and entertainment.     function send(path, payload) {

        var blob = new Blob([JSON.stringify(payload)], {
          type: 'text/plain; charset=UTF-8',
        });

      xhr.send(JSON.stringify(payload));
